malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This trust policy allows any unauthenticated Cognito user from any identity pool in any AWS account to assume the role, as there is no restriction on the audience (identity pool). This exposes the role to global unauthenticated users.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A secure trust policy should restrict both the authentication method and the specific identity pool (audience) using a Condition on cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud. This policy only restricts the authentication method, not the pool, violating proper scoping.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A developer might intend to allow all unauthenticated users in a single pool, but not globally across all AWS accounts.

package_info.why_malicious: The AWS Amplify CLI (and Amplify Studio) introduced a critical vulnerability in the IAM role trust policy templates it generated for Amplify projects. In certain versions, these templates created or modified IAM roles with trust policies that allowed any AWS account in the world to assume those roles via Cognito, without proper audience (identity pool) restrictions. This exposed privileged roles to global takeover, enabling attackers to gain access to AWS resources with the permissions of those roles. The vulnerability persisted for years, affecting a large number of projects and roles, and could be exploited remotely without access to the victim AWS account.

attack_chain.action: Amplify CLI or Studio creates or modifies IAM roles with overly permissive trust policies (variant one or two).
attack_chain.leads_to: IAM roles are globally assumable via Cognito.

attack_chain.action: Attacker discovers the ARN of a vulnerable role (e.g., via public code, deterministic naming, or web scraping).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker is able to target a specific role for assumption.

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates a Cognito identity pool in their own AWS account and generates a web identity token.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker is able to use the token to attempt role assumption.

attack_chain.action: Attacker calls sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity with the vulnerable role's ARN and their web identity token.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives STS credentials for the victim role.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the assumed role's credentials to access AWS resources with the permissions of the compromised role.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker achieves privilege escalation or data access in the victim AWS account.

IAM roles with names ending in authRole or unauthRole and no audience restriction in trust policy

IAM role trust policies lacking Condition on cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud

network_indicators: Unusual sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity API calls from external identity pools

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Enumerate all IAM roles in your AWS account and inspect their trust policies. Flag any role with Principal.Federated = cognito-identity.amazonaws.com and Action = sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity that does not include a Condition restricting cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud to a specific identity pool. Monitor CloudTrail for sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity events where the audience (identity pool) is not owned by your account, as this may indicate attempted exploitation. Pay special attention to roles with names ending in authRole or unauthRole, as these are commonly affected. Use automated scripts to audit trust policies and alert on any roles that are globally assumable via Cognito.
